public_rationale: Read in context, the claim is that the Senate did not act on preflight testing after 2023, and that policy shifted when Trump took office. Both parts hold. The Senate's May 2024 AI roadmap endorsed no specific regulations (e1), and by 2026 Congress still had passed no federal AI framework (e5). On January 20, 2025, Trump rescinded Biden's AI executive order (e2), then issued a new order focused on AI dominance (e3). One caveat: under Biden, NIST's AI Safety Institute signed voluntary deals in 2024 to get pre-release access to OpenAI and Anthropic models (e4). So 'nothing happened' overstates things if it is read to include voluntary executive-branch testing. The verdict depends on reading it as Senate or legislative inaction, which is how the passage frames it.
limitations: The outcome depends on reading 'nothing happened' as congressional inaction rather than all federal activity.
Voluntary pre-release testing under Biden (e4) partly undercuts a literal reading.
'Markedly' is a judgment, not a measurable threshold.

'Things changed markedly when Trump came to office' is read as a clear federal turn away from AI safety rules after January 20, 2025, such as revoking Biden's AI executive order.
Voluntary executive-branch testing deals made under Biden are not counted as the Senate 'doing something'. The reading leans on the Senate context, so it is flagged as a judgment call.

criteria.contradiction_condition: Records show Congress or the federal government adopted a preflight-testing system for AI models between 2023 and January 2025, or that federal AI policy did not change in a meaningful way when Trump took office.
